quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: Alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reactions slower.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast if a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle. This warns them of danger.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection when the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow. You should:

options.text: Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through the intersection before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive through carefully.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph could take up to ____ to come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need much longer distances to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph needs about 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: You are driving along a street and hear a siren. You cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait to make sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: An approaching driver fails to dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right edge of the road when a driver's bright headlights blind you. This helps you see the road and stay in your lane until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change when driving on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Other vehicles and motorcycles hide in this area. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on local streets and 5 seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: A motorist should know that a bicyclist operating on a roadway must:

options.text: Ride on the right side of the road.
Ride on the side of the road facing traffic.
Ride on either side of the road.
Ride on the side of the road with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must use a bike lane if one exists. If there is no bike lane, they must ride near the right edge of the road and move in the same direction as traffic.

questions.question: You must yield the right-of-way to an approaching vehicle when you are:
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to vehicles going straight or turning right. If another vehicle is already turning left at an intersection, wait for them to finish before entering. Drivers entering a traffic circle must yield to drivers already inside it.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle on the right if it is:

options.text: Turning into a driveway on the right.

questions.explanation: You can pass on the right in certain situations. You may pass on the right only if you can do so safely and do not drive on the shoulder or edge line. One safe situation is when the vehicle ahead is turning left.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the freeway shoulder only:

options.text: If you turn on your four-way flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: When driving past a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Be ready for the driver to open the door.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for the driver to open the door.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, expect the driver to open the door. Use extra caution when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: If traffic blocks you from crossing railroad tracks completely, proceed only when:

options.text: An approaching train is not moving too fast.
Your entire vehicle will clear the tracks.
At least half of your vehicle can cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire vehicle will clear the tracks.
questions.explanation: Always make sure your entire vehicle will clear the tracks. If traffic blocks the way, wait until there is enough space for your whole vehicle to cross.

questions.question: This sign is:
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. Slow down or stop if needed when you see this sign.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A car behind you starts to pass. You should:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Slow down a little and stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down a little and stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down slightly and stay to the right when another vehicle passes you. Once it is safely ahead, return to your normal speed.

questions.question: This sign warns you of:
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop when:

options.text: The road is wet or icy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet or icy.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads. They also increase on loose gravel or stones.
